text:
alex: spotted an onboarding spike  several folks hit 401s in the tutorial this morning after a customer's key rotation. looks like a mix of env-var confusion + project-scoped keys.

megan: details? which env var names are floating around?

alex: surprise: a community-contributed quickstart uses `REDWOOD_DEV_KEY`. public README uses `REDWOOD_API_KEY`, internal CLI examples show `REDWOOD_KEY`. chaos.

diego: that explains it. SDKs currently have different fallback orders. new users paste `REDWOOD_DEV_KEY` and SDKs ignore it -> generic 401.

soph: this is a good time to 1) standardize a single canonical name, 2) accept legacy names with a deprecation warning, and 3) ship a tiny CLI helper to print exact export lines for the user's shell.

megan: propose canonical = `REDWOOD_API_KEY`. accepted fallbacks: `REDWOOD_API_KEY`, `REDWOOD_KEY`, `REDWOOD_TOKEN`, `REDWOOD_DEV_KEY` (last one deprecated). When fallback hits a deprecated name, SDK logs: "Using deprecated env var REDWOOD_DEV_KEY; please set REDWOOD_API_KEY." Keep it one line.

diego: nice. also, stop retrying on 401s. current retry loop confuses users because they see delays. if server returns 401, SDK should surface an enriched error immediately with hints. e.g. "401 Unauthorized (AUTH_ROT or AUTH_SCOPE): possible causes: rotated key, project-scoped key, or wrong env var name. Try `rw auth export --format auto` to rehydrate your shell."

alex: +1. can we add an SDK error code field so the UI/support can route quickly? maybe `error.subcode = AUTH_SCOPE` or `AUTH_ROT` when server tags it.

soph: server-side: we'll add a detection rule. if presented key matches known legacy prefixes or was recently rotated, attach `rotation-suspected=true` and `subcode=AUTH_ROT`. otherwise, if token meta indicates project-scoped, set `subcode=AUTH_SCOPE`. SDK reads the subcode and renders targeted help.

megan: sampleapp README updates: include bash, PowerShell, CMD, and fish examples. small snippet for PowerShell: `$env:REDWOOD_API_KEY = "rw_..."`. CMD: `set REDWOOD_API_KEY=rw_...`. fish: `set -x REDWOOD_API_KEY rw_...`.

diego: for the CLI helper `rw auth export` let's make `--format auto|bash|ps1|cmd|fish`. `auto` detects shell from $SHELL or `ps` on Windows. Output should be just the commands so users can copy/paste. also include `--show-scope` to indicate if the key is project vs org scoped.

alex: support blurb to add to the onboarding checklist: "If you see 401 after rotation: 1) verify env var name is REDWOOD_API_KEY; 2) run `rw auth export --format auto` and paste the commands; 3) if error persists, ask user whether key was created with project scope and recommend generating an org-scoped key; 4) check for deprecated env var names in their repo (REDWOOD_DEV_KEY)."

soph: i'll open a tiny RFC for a shared env-resolution library we can import in all sdks so fallback lists stay consistent. also will add the richer 401 mapping.

megan: i'll patch sampleapp and the tutorial repo to remove `REDWOOD_DEV_KEY` and add a note about key scopes.

cred-bot: rotation-log: key rotated by ops@foo-corp at 2026-02-15T08:44:10Z; old_prefix=rw_oldX9; new_prefix=rw_newZ7; affected_clients=3

diego: timeline: SDK PR for parity + no-retry-on-401 + enriched error this week. `rw auth export` CLI PR next day. docs/sampleapp cleanup immediate. link PRs in the support ticket and ping once deployed.

alex: thanks all  these are low-risk changes but will cut a ton of initial friction. :thumbsup:
